notes.PURPOSE: A THROWAWAY LOCAL NETWORK for exercising the RandomX-path consensus rules end to end. It is NOT embedded in any binary and NOT a network anyone joins: it is run with `zycordd --params docs/localnet/params.randomx-localnet.json`, which is the one code path that takes an arbitrary parameter file and is deliberately given no seeds. Everything here is devnet's parameter set with two changes -- the work function and the key schedule -- because the point is to change the PoW path and nothing else. A local net that also moved the block time or the gas schedule would be measuring a different regime and could not be read against a devnet run.
notes.pow_engine: randomx-v1, and this is the whole reason the file exists. devnet runs dev-blake3, so until this recipe there was no network in the tree that drove the REAL work function through the node: not the keyed dataset, not the 256 MiB per-epoch caches, not the mining pause at a re-key. Those are the things a unit test over the blob cannot reach, because they are properties of the engine rather than of the encoding. Running this needs a binary built with `make build-randomx`; a binary without the tag REFUSES to start against this file rather than falling back to dev-blake3, which is the one-directional safety property spec/params.devnet.json's pow_engine note sets out.
notes.randomx_key_interval: 16 with a lag of 2, against devnet's 64/8 and mainnet's 2048/64. THE BOUNDARY IS THE THING THIS FILE EXISTS TO REACH. At target_block_seconds of 5 the first re-key lands at height 18, about 90 seconds in, and every 16 blocks -- roughly 80 seconds -- after that. On mainnet the same event is one every seventeen hours, which is why nothing routinely observes it. A run of a few minutes here crosses several boundaries, so the dataset rebuild, the mining pause and the fact that verification continues across it are exercised by ordinary use rather than by a test somebody has to remember to write. The 1:8 lag-to-interval ratio is preserved from both shipped networks on purpose: the ratio is what the lag MEANS -- slack inside one interval so the key a height needs was settled before that height could be mined -- and params.Validate refuses a lag at or above the interval outright.
notes.chain_id: 1337, the id spec/chain-ids.json allocates as 'ephemeral' for exactly this: throwaway local networks that are respun freely and on which no value is ever held. It is shared with devnet deliberately rather than allocated a new id. An ephemeral entry pins no genesis, so spec.CheckChainID has nothing to compare and permits both, which is the carve-out that keeps a routine parameter edit here from firing the respin refusal. The two networks still cannot talk: the handshake compares the GENESIS ID, and a different pow_engine and key schedule is a different consensus root is a different genesis (R3-1). Sharing the id costs nothing precisely because nothing is denominated on either.
notes.genesis_time: 1788652800 (2026-09-06T00:00:00Z). It is a fixed round UTC value rather than a launch date because this network has no launch: it is reset from genesis on every run, and a fixed value is what makes `zcd genesis --params <this file>` reproducible so two developers can confirm they are on the same local net. Reset the data directory rather than moving this.
notes.INHERITED: Every other value is devnet's and means what spec/params.devnet.json's notes say it means. Read that file for them; repeating them here would create two copies to drift apart.
